speaker: alse_pinder
text: Here is the twist of cloves, Master Shakespeare. Two pence, as you gave me on the stair. The boy weighed them with a thumb on the beam till I bade him take it off.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thank you, Alse. Lay them by the trencher. I will enter the two pence when the week is reckoned, and I will not enter it twice.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Two pence for dry buds, and three candlesticks down from your chamber with the wicks drowned. I have eyes, Master Shakespeare. I can count to three without chalk. I am not spending the count on a man who has not slept. You will hear it when you can hear.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The tallow is my own. The count, when you make it, will be a true one. Last night was not the girl.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: It is the full moon by the almanac. A tooth that gathers while the moon waxes comes to a head when the circle is full.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then by morning it might have the courtesy to wane with the rest of the sky. Today it only has to last an old Roman.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The penny loaf is still a thumb short of the notch. I cut you the middle, where the knife went easy.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Threepence the meal. Dip the bread if the jaw is proud. You paid your sixpence on Monday. Do not mix these buds in with it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Two pence is the cloves. Sixpence was the firing. They are not the same coin. The clove answers once the oil warms, and that is enough for two acts.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Tomorrow the term opens, and the streets will be black with gowns. Today is the Roman, and you say he is done by the fourth. Eat the soft of it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Shall I set a fresh candle for tonight, sir, or all three?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: One, Alse. Tonight I mean to sleep when the moon is over the close. The sheet can stay as Monday left it.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: Monday the shuttle went to Norton Folgate and came back. The loom does not ask what the moon is doing. I was at the board by dark, as I said I would be.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The moon can do as it likes. I have an old Roman at two. He is done in the fourth act, and then I am home.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Home, and one candle, as you have said. I am not heating a second for a man who walked the floor on three.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The soft of the loaf is on his side. I did not set a crust. The notch is still a full thumb short, and the price is still a penny.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No crust. The left side takes a clove and nothing harder. Two pence, Alse, and you have brought them.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I have the two pence in my head with the threepence, and they are not married. Eat the soft of it.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: I am a weaver, not a barber. The moon is printed in the almanac. Your gum is not my loom.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then do not turn barber at my trencher. The clove is in. The Roman can speak around it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: If the buds were light, the boy is not to be paid again. He took his thumb off the beam when I told him.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No second payment. Two pence is the price, and it is paid, and it will be written once, at the reckoning.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Once. I will know if the book says twice. The firing was Monday. These buds are not the firing.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: My own board is threepence, and I am not in his book. The moon is enough sky for a Wednesday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Enough sky. One candle. The sheet upstairs is Monday's, and it stays Monday's until I have slept.
